surprises.head: San Jose kept finding open men against Anton Forsberg
surprises.body: Forsberg allowed 5 goals on 25 shots, worth 1.7 expected goals: 3.3 more than expected, though three of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 50 starts.

surprises.head: San Jose couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

surprises.body: With chances like these, Los Angeles would win about 70 games in 100. San Jose won anyway.

story.head: The Sharks cash in
paras: Ivar Stenberg picked up his first NHL point. Adrian Kempe struck first for the Kings on the power play late in the first. It was a busy second period. Tyler Toffoli made it 1-1 for San Jose on the power play early in the period, and Kiefer Sherwood put the Sharks up 2-1 midway through the period. Nolan Allan scored his first goal for San Jose less than three minutes later to make it 3-1. Quinton Byfield cut San Jose’s lead to 3-2 on the power play with just two seconds left in the second. Igor Chernyshov stretched the lead to 4-2 early in the third. Erik Haula scored his first goal for Los Angeles midway through the period to pull the Kings within one. Artemi Panarin made it 4-4 with five minutes left. Chernyshov won it with his second goal of the night in overtime. Erik Gustafsson made his Kings debut, after two seasons with the Red Wings, and picked up an assist. Chernyshov added an assist for a three-point night.

The Kings had the better of the chances and hit four posts and the crossbar twice, but the Sharks made theirs count. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Kings win about seven in ten. Yaroslav Askarov made 31 saves for the Sharks, and Anton Forsberg allowed five goals on 25 shots. The Sharks moved to 2-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Kings dropped to 0-1-1 but climbed out of last place in the NHL.

items.text: Artemi Panarin scored again against San Jose, and has seven goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Mats Zuccarello extended his point streak against San Jose to six games.
The Sharks’ Darnell Nurse played his 800th NHL game.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
